reason: The cited evidence (E1) shows that increasing Al content in CoCrNiAlX alloys leads to a dense Al2O3 film that prevents oxidation, but it does not address boride-based components, hot-dip aluminization as a surface treatment, or resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion. The key premises about the intervention, substrate, and corrosion environment are unsupported by the provided evidence.
premises: Hot-dip aluminization can form a uniform, thin alumina film on boride-based components.
A dense, continuous Al2O3 layer acts as a chemically inert, diffusion-resistant barrier against molten aluminum.
Naturally formed oxide scales on boride-based components are loose and non-protective.
The alumina film will adhere well to the boride substrate.
The protective mechanism observed in CoCrNiAlX alloys (dense Al2O3 preventing oxidation) translates to corrosion resistance in molten aluminum.
